title: Wasteful Arsenal held by Borussia Dortmund
summary: Match report as Arsenal are denied victory by Borussia Dortmund in a Champions League encounter at the Emirates Stadium; Viktor Gyokeres scored a spectacular opener but Maximilian Beier equalised as the Gunners
content:
Match report as Arsenal are denied victory by Borussia Dortmund in a Champions League encounter at the Emirates Stadium; Viktor Gyokeres scored a spectacular opener but Maximilian Beier equalised as the Gunners wasted a string of chances Arsenal were punished for failing to take their chances for the second game in a row as Maximilian Beier clinched a 1-1 draw for Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League.

Viktor Gyokeres gave Arsenal an early lead with a stunning strike from distance but the game followed a similar pattern to Saturday's 2-2 draw with Newcastle as they were unable to capitalise on a one-sided first half before conceding after the break.

Dortmund's leveller came when Beier slotted a clinical finish past Kepa Arrizabalaga, standing in for the injured David Raya, following a rampaging run from defender Joane Gadou.

Arsenal racked up 30 shots and had a string of chances to win it in the closing stages, hitting the woodwork through Jurrien Timber's deflected cut-back and again through Declan Rice's low shot.

Gyokeres also spurned opportunities, firing over from close range from Martin Odegaard's pass shortly before half-time, then heading awkwardly wide from a few yards

content:
A defiant Borussia Dortmund side held firm under heavy pressure to earn a valuable point away to Arsenal in the Champions League.

Viktor Gyökeres opened the scoring beautifully, Maxi Beier leveled the score in the 55th minute and Gregor Kobel produced a string of top-drawer saves to weather Arsenal's late push, leaving BVB in a strong seventh spot in the standings.

The match got off to a spectacular start, with an absolute screamer opening the scoring in the 10th minute.

Viktor Gyökeres, usually Arsenal's second-choice striker behind Kai Havertz this season, found himself with a bit of space just outside the box and decided to try his luck.

His effort had plenty of topspin, sailed over the players in front of him and dipped at just the right moment to fly into the back of the net.

title: Ref chief Webb backs process around Yoro sending off despite successful appeal
summary: In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb analyses Man Utd defender Leny Yoro's sending off vs Liverpool - now  overturned on appeal - as audio of how the o
content:
In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Pro Ref chief refereeing officer Howard Webb analyses Man Utd defender Leny Yoro's sending off vs Liverpool - now overturned on appeal - as audio of how the officials handled the incident in real time is revealed Referees' chief Howard Webb has backed the process of the officials who sent off Manchester United defender Leny Yoro at Liverpool - despite the red card being overturned on appeal.

Yoro, sent off after eight minutes of Sunday's 4-0 defeat at Anfield, was due to face a one-match ban for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity when he brought down Alexander Isak outside the box and he was in on goal.

However, United have had the suspension lifted after a successful claim of wrongful dismissal, the FA said on Tuesday.

The independent commission will publish the written reasons in "due course".

In the latest edition of Match Officials Mic'd Up, Webb, chief refereeing officer at Pro Ref, described the on-field decision from referee Samuel Barrott as "decisive" and said the point of contention was around whether Isak would beat United goalkeeper Senne Lammens to the ball.

title: Yoro has red card overturned despite ref's chief Webb backing decision
summary:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak
Manchester United reporter in LisbonPublished24 November 2026, 15:59 GMTUpdated 32 minutes agoThe Football Assoc
content:
Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak Manchester United reporter in LisbonPublished24 November 2026, 15:59 GMTUpdated 32 minutes agoThe Football Association has overturned Leny Yoro's red card from Manchester United's defeat by Liverpool on Sunday – even though referee's chief Howard Webb has backed the decision to send the defender off.

Yoro was dismissed by referee Sam Barrott for bringing down Liverpool forward Alexander Isak just eight minutes into the Anfield clash.

Isak had run onto a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch which meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if the Liverpool man had not been brought down by Yoro just outside the area.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said.

title: Bundesliga planning new Saturday night kick-off time from 2029/30
summary: The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle. According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marque
content:
The Bundesliga could introduce a new Saturday evening kick-off time from the 2029/30 season as part of the next domestic television rights cycle.

According to Bild, plans are being drawn up to stage five marquee Bundesliga fixtures per season at 20:30 CET on Saturday evenings.

The proposal was reportedly well received at a meeting of the 36 Bundesliga and 2.

Bundesliga clubs in Frankfurt at the beginning of October, with the prospect of attracting larger television audiences in a prime-time slot appealing to potential broadcasters.

Crucially, the traditional Saturday 15:30 kick-off time would remain unaffected, as would the existing 18:30 slot.

title: Bayern hold constructive talks with Musiala's representatives amid ongoing tensions
summary: Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage. As per Sky Germa
content:
Following weeks of public debate surrounding Jamal Musiala's health and contractual situation, Bayern Munich have taken a step towards easing tensions with the German international's entourage.

As per Sky Germany, Musiala's agents Christian Schmid and Tobias Altschäffl met with Jan-Christian Dreesen, Herbert Hainer and Max Eberl at Säbener Straße on Tuesday, with neither Uli Hoeneß nor Karl-Heinz Rummenigge - both of whom have publicly raised concerns over Musiala's situation in recent weeks - present at the meeting.

The discussions are said to have been constructive, with both parties keen to improve communication behind closed doors following the recent public exchanges.

Having made his return to action against Köln on Friday, it is said that Musiala will now be given time to focus on his football, with the Bayern hierarchy keen to alleviate some of the pressure on the 23-year-old.

In the meantime, the attacking midfielder may have to take on a more integral role, with Harry Kane's absence, the unavailability of Michael Olise, and doubts over Luis Diaz ahead of the trip to Lille on Wednesday.

(Photo by Marco Rosi - SS Lazio/Getty Images) Ultras of Lazio’s Curva Nord have announced that they will temporarily lift their Stadio Olimpico boycott for their Serie A clash at home against Atalanta on December 6, but not all supporters agree with the decision.

Lazio supporters have been boycotting their home matches since the beginning of the calendar year in protest of owner Claudio Lotito.

Fans are demanding that Lotito sell the club and had promised that they would not return to the stadium, aside from derby fixtures, until he had done so.

Despite home season tickets plummeting to around 3,000 season and away supporters regularly outnumbering home fans in the Stadio Olimpico in 2026-27, Lazio have surged to the top of the Serie A table and remain unbeaten after the first 12 league matches of the season.
